page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r6.large is a memory-optimized virtual server instance based on the KVM hypervisor. It features 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 1 physical Intel Xeon 8269CY core with hyper-threading enabled. The processor operates at a base clock speed of 2.5 GHz and includes a 35 MB L3 cache. The instance is configured with 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it operates with a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations indicate that the ecs.r6.large exhibits limited processing and memory throughput capabilities. In stress-ng testing, both single-core and multi-core CPU performance fall into the bottom 25% and 10% categories respectively. Memory bandwidth tests show a read-only small block cached speed of 96.46 GB/sec and a large block uncached write speed of 11.37 GB/sec, both placing in the bottom 10% of tested hardware. Similarly, database operations and Redis SET performance of 1.67 million operations per second are positioned in the lower tier, reflecting constraints in raw execution speed despite the dedicated CPU allocation.

The primary tradeoff of the ecs.r6.large is its generous memory allocation relative to its modest compute performance. While the Intel Xeon architecture supports advanced instruction sets like AVX-512 and AES, the low physical core count and weak benchmark scores limit its utility for compute-intensive tasks. This instance is best suited for memory-bound workloads with low CPU utilization, such as small-scale caching layers, lightweight database hosting, or memory-intensive background processes that do not require high throughput or local storage.
